review_notes: I read the whole file and Separation.lean, which defines `Separates`. The file's definitions are `Positive`, `Valid`, `HasBoundedWitnesses` and `SetSeparates`. All of them are specific to this project's finite-witness characterization of language generation. They are predicates on families of sets and witness assignments. I know of no Mathlib, Batteries or core concept with the same meaning. `SetSeparates` is a deliberate generalization of `Separates`, because it uses a set-valued assignment `P`. `setSeparates_finset` links the two, so I do not count them as competing versions. `Valid` and `HasFiniteWitnesses` appear to unfold to the same thing, as `Valid.hasFiniteWitnesses := ⟨T, h⟩` suggests. Both are project-internal and not Mathlib, and I did not read `HasFiniteWitnesses` itself in Characterization.lean. `exists_countable_same_core` and `setSeparates_iff_countable` are theorems, so duplicating Mathlib results would be out of scope for this rubric. I did not search Mathlib for an equivalent of `exists_countable_same_core`. I found no justified duplicate-concept finding.
